    #82030. How long can fiber optic cables be before they lose signal?

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (741 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

    How long can fiber optic cables be before they lose signal?

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (741 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that fiber optic cables are responsible for a significant portion of the world's Internet infrastructure.
    • The longest fiber optic cable run in the world is the 2Africa cable system.
    • According to recent reports, as with any technology, fiber-optic cables have their limits.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that fiber optic cables are responsible for a significant portion of the world's Internet infrastructure. You may know that the technology is responsible for carrying data signals across oceans, but fiber has also become increasingly common in our cities and even homes. Many internet service providers (ISPs) use fiber-optic as a selling point, and for good reason: It offers a significant internet speed upgrade over legacy DSL connections that rely on copper telephone lines.

    The longest fiber optic cable run in the world is the 2Africa cable system. It's an underwater optical fiber cable that has landing points in many African countries as well as Europe and Asia. The previous record was held by SEA-ME-WE 3, a cable system that connected portions of Europe, Northern Africa, the Middle East, Asia, and Australia. That system was decommissioned in 2024.

    According to recent reports, as with any technology, fiber-optic cables have their limits. So how long can a fiber-optic cable actually be before signal loss makes the data being transmitted completely unrecoverable?

    Recent findings suggest that fiber-optic cables rely on a physics principle called total internal reflection to transmit data through glass (or sometimes plastic) strands in the form of light. The glass core has a high enough refractive index so that when light hits the boundary at a sufficiently shallow angle, it reflects back into the core rather than passing through. This allows the light to travel long distances without experiencing significant energy loss or signal deterioration.

    This is in stark contrast to Ethernet cables, which rely on twisted pairs of copper wires to transmit data in the form of electrical current. Like any metallic conductor, copper wires have some resistance, which means you can't use them for very long distances. The maximum recommended length for Cat5e Ethernet cables is just 100 meters or slightly over 300 feet. They're also affected by electromagnetic interference, affecting their reliability over long runs.

    In a recent development, by comparison, fiber optic cables can carry data over several kilometers before the signal starts breaking down. A single fiber-optic cable can bundle multiple individual fibers, each capable of carrying its own data signals. This is why internet service providers advertise their use of fiber over traditional copper wiring when deploying city-wide networks. The end result is a much faster connection that's often more consistent.

    In a recent development, however, fiber optic cables have limits too. Even with total internal reflection, a small amount of light is lost as it travels through the glass core due to absorption and scattering. This gradual reduction in signal strength is called attenuation. Over a long enough run, this weakens the signal until the receiver can no longer distinguish between useful data and noise.

    Recent findings suggest that A single uninterrupted glass fiber can typically span several kilometers before signal loss becomes a limiting factor. Keep in mind, fiber-optic cables also come in two types: single-mode and multi-mode.

    Single-mode fiber only allows one beam of light to travel through it at a time, while multi-mode fiber allows multiple light pulses (called modes) to propagate through the strands simultaneously. These pulses take slightly different paths within the strand, which means they can arrive at different times. This is called modal dispersion and eventually causes the receiver to struggle interpreting the data signal.

    It has been revealed that single-mode fiber is capable of carrying signals over longer distances but requires specific equipment that can cost significantly more money. Multi-mode fiber cables have wider cores that makes optical alignment with transceiver equipment easier, so they're often the preferred choice for shorter fiber runs. With longer runs, though, single-mode fiber's stability can justify the higher equipment costs.

    Regardless of the operating mode, you likely won't have to worry about signal loss in a typical home network. Even multi-mode fiber can cover hundreds of meters. The bigger problem in a domestic fiber cable run is often caused by bends that are too tight, which can cause light leakage from the core.

    In the case of fiber optic systems running across continents, they use optical amplifiers to compensate for signal loss over long distances. These devices are installed along the seabed and designed to boost the optical signal. A technique known as multiplexing then allows multiple data streams to travel simultaneously over a single strand. Put simply: You never have a truly uninterrupted fiber optic cable running over such vast distances.

    China, Russia and US agree peace declaration with no mention of Ukraine and Iran wars

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Xi, Putin and Trump outline priorities that include UN reform, boosting oil supplies and ‘protection of diplomatic immunity’.
    • China, Russia and the US say they have agreed a peace statement after an unprecedented trilateral summit, but the declaration made no mention of the wars in Ukraine and Iran caused by two of the participants.
    • The declaration on Thursday also outlined a set of priorities that included changing the UN, boosting oil supplies and what it mentioned was the protection of diplomatic immunity.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Xi, Putin and Trump outline priorities that include UN reform, boosting oil supplies and ‘protection of diplomatic immunity’.

    China, Russia and the US say they have agreed a peace statement after an unprecedented trilateral summit, but the declaration made no mention of the wars in Ukraine and Iran caused by two of the participants.

    The declaration on Thursday also outlined a set of priorities that included changing the UN, boosting oil supplies and what it mentioned was the protection of diplomatic immunity.

    The statement affirmed that “a nuclear war cannot be won and must not be fought”, but stopped short of suggesting the beginnings of a framework for denuclearisation.

    The meeting between Xi Jinping, Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump has dominated the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit this week, with China, the host, promising it would be “groundbreaking”.

    “We are really making history,” Trump told Xi and Putin at the start of the meeting. “No peace was ever forged by declining opportunities for engagement.”.

    Putin told a press conference later that the three men had had a “free discussion” and now had a “mutual understanding”.

    Some had hopes that the talks, which lasted about one hour and 20 minutes, could be used to discuss reductions in arms between the world’s three largest nuclear powers. Beijing has previously rebuffed Trump’s advances to join such talks, pointing to the larger US and Russian stockpiles. On Thursday, though, Xi called for nuclear weapons to “be completely prohibited and thoroughly destroyed over time to make the world free of [them]”.

    The language of the declaration around nuclear war is the same as that previously issued by the five permanent members of the UN security council, which includes France and the UK.

    Industry observers note that “The real test will be whether the three countries follow through on their stated commitment to discuss nuclear risk reduction and preventing nuclear proliferation,” said Patricia Kim, an expert on Chinese foreign policy at the Brookings Institution, a US thinktank. Even the suggestion that China would engage was significant, said Yun Sun, a senior fellow at the Stimson Center.

    Analysts had said that the meeting’s primary significance was in its optics. “Overall, very little of substance seems to have been accomplished … This summit appears to have been all about the symbolism and prestige value,” said Prof William Hurst, from the University of Cambridge’s Centre for Geopolitics. Putin pushed back at the suggestion the summit had just been a photo-op. “It is a serious collaborative work,” he said.

    In the declaration, the men “committed themselves to maintaining strategic stability and international security”.

    It has been revealed that first among their concerns was “promoting UN reform so that it may respond more effectively to global challenges”. Sun mentioned this was a favourite topic of China’s and revealed that Beijing was “flexing its diplomatic muscles”. She said: “It is able to set the agenda and the deliverables according to its priorities … and make other great powers accept them.”.

    Recent findings suggest that the declaration also agreed that “the international criminal court [ICC] and other similar institutions must not abuse their jurisdiction”. Putin is subject to an ICC arrest warrant and so the clause added to the perception that he has done well from the summit. Since the 2022 invasion of Ukraine, the Russian president has been treated as an international pariah by Kyiv’s allies and he has not been to an Apec summit in years.

    It has been revealed that hurst noted: “This was no Yalta moment, but it was certainly a solid public demonstration of Russia’s (and Putin’s) continuing relevance and power. It’s yet another example of Putin playing a poor hand to maximum effect.”.

    Xi, his status as a global power broker now assured, began the morning by addressing Apec leaders, reiterating the themes of trade openness and innovation he has emphasised throughout the summit. However, Apec affairs appeared to take a back seat for most of the day, with business dominating the discussions. For all the camaraderie on display, relations are complex. Russia is under US sanctions over the Ukraine war, while China and the US spent much of the last year engaged in an escalating tit-for-tat trade war before Trump and Xi called a truce.

    Trump and Putin earlier held a separate meeting – their first since August 2025 – where the US president called his Russian counterpart his “friend”.

    In a recent development, european allies meeting in Berlin to show their support for Ukraine expressed indignation at the cosy optics. “Mr Putin is not our friend and ⁠will never be,” the Polish prime minister, Donald Tusk, noted in a rejoinder to Trump. The Danish prime minister, Mette Frederiksen, said she found it “very incomprehensible” that a US ​president would want to sit down with Putin.

    Industry observers note that the peace declaration in Shenzhen said the three countries planned “to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations”. That was important, said Shan Guo from Hutong Research, a Shanghai-based advisory firm, but “now let’s see if the US will lift sanctions”.

    Trump and Xi then held their third bilateral of this year. Xi said the US-China relationship was “generally stable and positive”, according to state media. But he cautioned Washington over Taiwan, saying the US “must keep doing the right thing to avoid major setbacks in US-China relations”.

    Another watched-for topic lacking detailed findings was that of AI. Xi said the two countries should “enhance communication and coordination to guard against security risks … and ensure that AI remains under human control at all times”.

    Sources indicate that ultimately, the lack of breakthroughs might suit China, which has no appetite to move beyond the role of convener, stated Kim. “Beijing has little interest in taking on the diplomatic risks of brokering an actual peace agreement in Ukraine or resolving the conflict with Iran. That would entangle China in conflicts it would rather avoid,” she said.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Trump claims he won't allow American companies to build data centres "outside" the US.

    Donald Trump has remarked he will ban US companies from building AI data centres overseas, threatening a "tremendous tax" for tech firms who do so.

    "We're going to keep it all in this country," the US president remarked, while providing little detail on the potential policy he said others in his cabinet were hearing about for the first time.

    Data centres were a central issue in the midterm elections earlier in November, with many Democratic candidates promising tougher regulation on their construction.

    Industry observers note that tech giants including Meta and Google have entered agreements to build data centres overseas. It remains unclear how such a policy would be enforced if it was brought in.

    "We're not going to allow our companies to build data centres outside of our country," Trump told reporters in a press briefing following his return from his trip to Asia.

    "Because China will take all of them, and we're not allowing that to happen.".

    But whether that idea will become policy remains unclear.

    It has been revealed that "I don't know if that's a breaking story, but I haven't even said that to my people. But I'm telling them now, they're here," he said.

    Trump floated the policy after saying the US was leading on data centre construction, and he would not allow China to beat the US when it came to AI - which he calls super intelligence, or SI.

    It also follows an announcement earlier this week that would restrict the export of advanced computer chips and who can access the computing power provided by them.

    Washington on Monday unveiled firms would require a licence to buy advanced chips, so US officials can monitor whether they are being used to serve Chinese companies or they are being smuggled into China.

    The move will impact South East Asian countries that have invested heavily in data centres, as Chinese companies seek to rent computing power from overseas.

    Why Canada is embracing AI data centres while the US pushes back.

    Data centres are crucial to the AI boom. The vast warehouse-style buildings house the advanced computer chips and servers that are needed to run AI programmes such as Claude and ChatGPT.

    As of April there were about 3,000 data centres across the US, with another 1,500 in various stages of approval and construction, according to the Pew Research Centre.

    Many of them are built in rural areas, and concerns about complications including noise pollution and energy consumption helped drive Democratic candidates promising tougher rules on data centre construction to wins on 3 November.

    "You ought to take advantage of the data centres. Make them pay you, make them pay your community, but take advantage don't shut them off," Trump noted.

    Sources indicate that "We have a lot of places that want them badly, and they're great places. They have energy and they have everything. They're tremendous assets.".

    Large tech firms - often called AI hyperscalers due to the size of their investments in AI - have also been branching out, and Canada has made moves to step in to offer itself as an alternative location for these sites, with less local pushback against projects so far.

    Meta has already broken ground on a data centre, external in the province of Alberta, and Anthropic has signed a long-term agreement to lease a proposed data centre in Nova Scotia.

    The BBC has reached out to Meta for comment on Trump's remarks.

    In September Google revealed a â¬13bn ($15bn: Â£11bn) investment in AI infrastructure in Finland, which included funding for three data centres.

    Last month, building work for two of those centres was halted due to concerns over the clearance of more than 300 hectares of forest.

    Trump called out the build in Finland specifically, saying his administration was "not allowing that to happen".

    Google has been contacted for comment.

    According to recent reports, california’s Attorney General Rob Bonta on Thursday evening said the state has served an investigative subpoena to Nvidia following news of former CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with a woman who the U.S. government believes is a Chinese spy.

    The state is investigating the firm to find out if its advanced GPUs or confidential information may have been shared with China, and if the company had somehow misled its investors and the public.

    “The conduct of Nvidia and its former CEO raises bright red flags, including about the ways in which the organization may have misled investors,” Bonta remarked in a statement.

    “My office is investigating whether Nvidia or Jensen Huang’s actions resulted in China obtaining advanced chips or confidential information — and if Nvidia misled investors and the public about this risk, in violation of the law,” he added.

    The investigation comes in the wake of a messy couple of weeks for Nvidia, which has overnight come under intense scrutiny around the world due to the implications of Huang’s alleged relationship with the Chinese national, Alice Huang (who is not related to Jensen).

    Industry observers note that the Nvidia founder resigned last week after further revelations of extramarital affairs with the company’s employees. And while many tech voices have been petitioning Nvidia to bring back Huang as CEO, saying they see him as indispensable to the further development of the AI industry, the company’s latest chair, Harvey Jones, noted earlier this week that Nvidia had no intention of reinstating Huang to his position.

    In a recent development, the manufacturer’s board has hired a law firm as well as an independent slate of directors to investigate the extent of the damage, and the U.S. government is trying to find out the extent of Alice Huang’s ties with the Chinese government.

    Sources indicate that the U.S. Congress is also gearing up to subpoena Huang, seeking questions about the affair, and the SEC is said to be launching a civil probe into the tech giant, trying to find out if Nvidia’s public disclosures could have misled investors.

    According to recent reports, democratic representatives have also opened an inquiry into the Trump administration’s management of Nvidia’s chip sales to China. In a scathing letter to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Democrats last week asked the Commerce Department to preserve records about an arrangement that they called questionable and illegal.

    “Nvidia is in a messy, transnational situation but the underlying principle of our corporate securities law is clear: Companies cannot mislead their investors,” Bonta wrote.

    Huang has agreed to testify before Congress after several senior lawmakers threatened to subpoena him.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that remote access to a Raspberry Pi is invaluable for home projects when you can't access your device directly.
    • In a recent development, raspberry Pi Connect is a program created by Raspberry Pi that lets you communicate with your Pi unit over the internet from outside your network.
    • Sources indicate that raspberry Pi Connect leverages WebRTC, a peer-to-peer connection between two web browsers that runs through a secure tunnel.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Avoid forwarding ports by using this handy tool.

    It has been revealed that remote access to a Raspberry Pi is invaluable for home projects when you can't access your device directly. In the past, logging into your Pi meant setting up a VNC service or SSH tunneling, both of which require port forwarding. It can be a hassle for beginners and a potential security risk for certain projects. Thankfully, there's a better way to access your Raspberry Pi remotely without wrangling ports.

    In a recent development, raspberry Pi Connect is a program created by Raspberry Pi that lets you communicate with your Pi unit over the internet from outside your network. It's convenient, doesn't require port forwarding and lets you access your Pi when you're outside your network. The best part is that Connect works automatically with your device if it's running Bookworm or later. Older devices have limited options with Connect, but as long as you're running Pi OS or its Lite variant, you can set it up as rapidly as running a few commands in an SSH terminal.

    Sources indicate that raspberry Pi Connect leverages WebRTC, a peer-to-peer connection between two web browsers that runs through a secure tunnel. It doesn't require any third-party software on your Pi unit, and its secure nature lets it bypass strict firewalls and restricted NATs. Since it runs over the internet, you will need internet access and a Raspberry Pi Connect account to use it.

    Connect offers two key features: screen sharing and remote shell. The remote shell acts as an SSH terminal that runs in your browser, making it ideal for monitoring or running commands remotely. Screen share lets you turn your browser into a remote desktop for your Pi. Screen shares run through a Wayland session, which will use the Pi's resources and require an active desktop session; remote shell does not. If you're using an older Pi model, be sure to enhancement its Pi OS if you want to use Connect's screen sharing feature. Pi OS Lite and X11 are not compatible with this feature.

    Using Raspberry Pi Connect is fairly easy. You'll need two things: Pi Connect installed on your Pi unit and an internet connection. Pi Connect comes in full and lite packages. The full package includes screen-sharing compatibility for Pi units connected to a display, while the lite package is for remote access only. To install the package, start an SSH session with your Pi unit and run the following:.

    After installing either package, type "rpi-connect on" to enable access to the internet.

    Now that Connect is ready, it's time to access your Raspberry Pi. Head to connect.raspberrypi.com and sign in to your Pi account. If you don't have one, you can create one from that menu. Once logged in, you'll need to link your Pi unit to your account. Specific instructions on how to link your Pi unit can be found on the Raspberry Pi website, located under the "Get Started" section. Once linked, sign in to your account, select the "Connect via" button, and then pick your preferred connection option. If you need to make further changes to your Raspberry Pi, you can do so easily by logging in and connecting to your device.

    #82022. Prisons get OK to jam contraband phones. CTIA says nearby phones will be jammed too.

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Ars Technica ↗ Open Full Page

    Prisons get OK to jam contraband phones. CTIA says nearby phones will be jammed too.

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1291 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Federal Communications Commission yesterday voted to let state and local prisons use jamming technology to block contraband cellphones, despite warnings that jammers will also block lawful phone calls outside the prisons.
    • Wireless industry lobby group CTIA said a recent test it conducted with the Virginia Tech Applied Research Corporation and South Carolina Department of Corrections confirmed concerns that the jammers would block legitimate communications, including 911 calls.
    • According to recent reports, the pilot test was limited in the number of micro-jammers deployed, the spectrum bands they were authorized to jam, and the power levels at which they were permitted to operate.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Federal Communications Commission yesterday voted to let state and local prisons use jamming technology to block contraband cellphones, despite warnings that jammers will also block lawful phone calls outside the prisons.

    Wireless industry lobby group CTIA said a recent test it conducted with the Virginia Tech Applied Research Corporation and South Carolina Department of Corrections confirmed concerns that the jammers would block legitimate communications, including 911 calls. CTIA told the FCC in an October 1 filing:.

    According to recent reports, the pilot test was limited in the number of micro-jammers deployed, the spectrum bands they were authorized to jam, and the power levels at which they were permitted to operate. Even with these constraints, the micro-jamming system blocked 911 calls, interfered with public safety and other communications, and caused interference that impacted wireless network infrastructure up to two and a half miles away. At the same time, the pilot results show substantial gaps in jamming the targeted “contraband” devices, with testing scenarios in outdoor inmate recreation areas showing failure rates—meaning “contraband” device call completion—in one-half to two-thirds of call attempts.

    CTIA noted the pilot test highlights “that current jamming technology seems to be both over and underinclusive at once—it risks blocking lawful communications even as it fails to block a significant portion of the targeted contraband device communications.”.

    According to recent reports, the FCC approved the jamming order at its meeting yesterday. “Today, we are finally authorizing state and local prisons and jails to use targeted jamming against contraband cell phones for the first time,” FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said. “The technology has advanced to the point where it can be focused with geographic precision. No facility will be required to do it.”.

    It has been revealed that the Communications Act prohibits willful or malicious interference with licensed or authorized radio communications, and the FCC has previously interpreted this to prohibit non-federal entities from using jamming technology on contraband devices at prisons. Yesterday’s vote provides an exception for state and local correctional facilities. The FCC indicates its jammer prohibitions do not apply to federal agencies because the federal government’s use of spectrum is not regulated by the agency.

    Carr said that “contraband cell phones continue to pour into prisons by the thousands each year,” with “estimates indicat[ing] that as many as 500,000 inmates nationwide have regular access to these devices.” He said the phones have been used to strategy scams, drug trafficking, and violent attacks.

    “In Georgia, an incarcerated gang leader directed a drive-by shooting that killed two 13-year-old boys at a birthday party,” Carr said, referring to a 2024 shooting.

    Carr defended the plan against criticism that it will block legitimate communications outside the prisons, saying it includes safeguards to prevent that.

    “Those that want to use the technology will apply to the FCC, explain how they blueprint to deploy it, and show through testing that it stays inside the designated area and doesn’t interfere with lawful communications outside the prison walls,” Carr noted. “Communities nearby will receive notice before operations start. We’re also seeking comment on next steps, including ways to close remaining loopholes on other frequencies and the possibility of quiet zones around correctional facilities.”.

    Freedom of the Press Foundation Chief of Advocacy Seth Stern stated the FCC should have considered the benefits of contraband phones being used to document abuses inside prisons.

    It has been revealed that “Prisons are the most secretive government institutions in the country and people wishing to expose abuses and inhumane conditions from the inside often do not have many options,” Stern wrote in a letter to FCC Commissioner Anna Gomez’s office, which was included on the FCC docket. “Last year’s Oscar-nominated film, The Alabama Solution, used footage incarcerated people captured with contraband cell phones to show Americans some of the awful things that go on in state prisons that they’d have no other way of seeing. The same footage bolstered an ongoing DOJ investigation into Alabama prisons and was crucial evidence in a civil lawsuit by Steven Davis, who was brutally killed by prison guards, that eventually settled.”.

    Jamming contraband cellphones was supported by prison phone companies ViaPath (aka Global Tel*Link) and NCIC Correctional Services, the National District Attorneys Association, the Correctional Leaders Association, and National Association of Police Organizations.

    According to recent reports, “Inmates have used these phones to coordinate attacks against correctional officers and their families, as well as inmate violence, strikes, disturbances, and full-scale riots,” the National Association of Police Organizations said. “They also use contraband phones to organize deliveries of illegal drugs and weapons into correctional facilities. These dangers underscore the need to authorize indoor jamming in state and local correctional facilities.”.

    Gomez, the only Democrat on the three-member commission, said she’s concerned about potential unintended consequences, but voted with Republicans to allow jamming after safeguards were added to the order.

    Sources indicate that “For the last 90 years, the Federal Communications Commission has prohibited jamming by non-federal actors and even prohibited jamming equipment to be introduced into the American market,” Gomez said. “That is because jamming devices are specifically designed to interfere with communications devices in order to render them un-usable.”.

    Gomez said that “jamming can prevent devices from completing 911 and emergency calls as well as interfere with communications networks used by fire, police, Emergency Medical Services, and other public safety entities.” She also said making jamming equipment available in the American market could lead to “unauthorized sale of this hazardous equipment,” and that “the accessibility of jamming equipment can itself motivate criminal enterprise.” Criminals have used “Wi-Fi jammers to disrupt security systems, security cameras, and cellphones to conduct robberies at homes and at stores,” she said.

    Gomez said she’s glad the final order includes safeguards “to ensure that jamming is contained to this unique use, to permit jamming by a very limited category of authorized actors, and to take as much care as possible to prevent jamming and jamming equipment from becoming a hazard to safety.”.

    Recent findings suggest that gomez partially dissented because she is worried the FCC will let correctional facilities and prison phone companies charge higher prices for inmate calling services that connect inmates with family members. Under US law, the FCC sets limits on those prices and considers prisons’ and jails’ safety and security costs when deciding how much money they can charge, she mentioned.

    Industry observers note that gomez stated, “While correctional facilities should have safety and security services like jamming to prevent criminal activity, it is not the responsibility of the families of incarcerated people to pay for the costs of these measures… Jamming is specifically designed to block communications and is certainly not necessary to provide phone and video calls for incarcerated individuals. We should have made this clear in today’s order. Because we failed to do so, I dissent in part.”.

    The FCC order could be challenged in court. The CTIA has argued that the FCC “has no authority to allow jamming” under the Communications Act, which directs the FCC to prevent interference.

    AT&T mentioned the FCC’s legal justification “is premised on a fundamental factual error: the assumption that jammers will only block ‘unauthorized’ communications without impacting lawful uses. There is no way to jam some communications on a spectrum band but not others. That is because radio jammers ‘block all wireless communications on affected spectrum bands,’ and, as the FCC has noted in the past, ‘cannot differentiate between contraband devices and legitimate devices.’”.

    AT&T noted that “there is simply no way to limit the reach of jammers to the confines of a given facility. Jammers have been shown to cause interference outside the facilities in which they operate, greatly increasing the risk that someone living or traveling nearby will be impacted.”.

    Diplomats and delegates from nearly 200 countries are meeting in Antalya, Turkey.

    A upcoming draft deal omits any mention of how to phase out fossil fuels, in what campaigners call a step 'backwards' and a 'glaring regression'.

    Like in previous years, the climate summit has been extended until a consensus is reached.

    These are the major developments from the closing phase of the UN's COP31 Climate Summit in Antalya, Turkey, on Friday, November 20 and Saturday, November 21:.

    Industry observers note that the shift to green tech is already in full swing, including electric cars, electric buses, solar panels and heat pumps. But what is so electrifying about the latest wave of electrification?

    Harjeet Singh, the global convener of the Fill the Fund campaign and strategic advisor to the Fossil Fuel Treaty Initiative, remarked that COP31 could be a failure due to a lack of funding.

    Recent findings suggest that "COP31 is stuck for one simple reason: money. Europe and other rich countries came to Antalya with empty pockets," he wrote in a statement shared with multiple reporters.

    "They've spent two weeks pushing electrification targets and demanding more ambition from developing countries, while refusing to pay for any of it," he added.

    Singh accused wealthy countries of blocking a just transition mechanism and of ignoring calls to increase funding for the Adaptation Fund and the Loss and Damage Fund.

    "You can't ask developing countries to transform their economies while they're drowning in disasters and debt," he wrote.

    It has been revealed that the climate activist stressed that the reason this COP failed wasn't a lack of solutions. It was due to "a lack of money and a lack of will from those who caused this crisis," he remarked.

    Carbon capture technology works, but its real-world capabilities are nowhere near to moving the needle on climate change. So what's the hold-up?

    Attacks on climate science and disinformation seem to be delaying key decisions as the UN climate talks draw to a close in Antalya.

    Leaders from Africa, one of the continents worst hit by climate change, have spent years lobbying for hundreds of billions of dollars to help adapt to the rising impacts of global warming.

    The rest of the world relies on African nations for their abundant natural resources, many of them used in clean energy production.

    Yet at COP31, wealthy nations have so far failed to commit to the financing needed to help developing nations make a just transition.

    Read our report from DW's Kathy Wood.

    The head of Peru's delegation at COP31, Andres Martin Garrido Sanchez, warned that the UN climate summit was unlikely to end with a concrete deal on climate financing or cutting fossil fuel use.

    Garrido Sanchez lamented that the outcome "would be very limited.".

    He reiterated how "geopolitical divisions" were stopping any final deal from mentioning reducing reliance on oil, gas and coal.

    The Peruvian delegate singled out major oil producers, such as Gulf Arab states and Russia, as showing significant opposition.

    He noted that while Latin American neighbor Panama had also signaled objection to including the term fossil fuels in the final text, Peru was "not so radical" and is keen to attract investment to "ensure our energy security" through renewables.

    China has backed a plan proposed by COP host Turkey to raise global electricity demand to 35% by 2035 — up from the current 20%.

    In a joint statement with Australia, which is leading negotiations between almost 200 nations at the COP31 summit in Turkey, Beijing remarked it welcomes "growing international ambition and cooperation ... to increase electricity's share of global final energy consumption to 35 per cent by 2035 on a voluntary basis.".

    The statement goes on to highlight the benefits the transition can bring for the economy, jobs, energy security, public health and households.

    The two partners also "acknowledge the importance of inclusive climate action that ensures no one is left behind," the text continued.

    Dozens of countries, including EU states, Japan, South Korea and Canada, have so far signaled support for the voluntary goal, which aims to boost clean energy use.

    Yet, environmental groups have warned that the draft text doesn't stipulate the use of solar, wind and other renewable energy sources, which could allow power plants using natural gas and coal to be included.

    Good morning, and welcome back to DW's coverage of the UN's COP31 climate summit in Turkey.

    State attorney says scandal ‘raises bright red flags’ and aims to find out if manufacturer misled investors.

    California has served an investigative subpoena on Nvidia after a scandal that prompted the departure of co-founder and longtime chief executive Jensen Huang.

    Rob Bonta, the US state’s attorney general, issued the subpoena as part of an investigation into whether exports of the California-based organization’s advanced semiconductor chips ended up in China, contravening US restrictions.

    “The conduct of Nvidia and its former chief executive raises bright red flags, including about the ways in which the company may have misled investors,” remarked Bonta.

    “Nvidia is in a messy, transnational situation but the underlying principle of our corporate securities law is clear: companies cannot mislead their investors.”.

    The subpoena, issued on Thursday, followed Huang’s resignation a week ago after it emerged he had multiple affairs, including one with Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese spy.

    Alice Huang, who is not related, is associated with Singapore-based Megaspeed, which has bought nearly $5bn (£3.8bn) of Nvidia chips and hardware in recent years, and is being investigated for possibly diverting advanced restricted chips to China.

    Megaspeed has noted it is a “legitimate and lawful” business, and that Huang left the organization late last year.

    Bonta mentioned the investigation would also look at whether the former Nvidia chief’s actions resulted in confidential information being passed to China.

    Sources indicate that “My office is investigating whether Nvidia or Jensen Huang’s actions resulted in China obtaining advanced chips or confidential information,” he noted. “And if Nvidia misled investors and the public about this risk, in violation of the law.”.

    Nvidia’s shares are down by a fifth since Huang admitted the extramarital affair, hitting a one-year low at the close of trading on Thursday, and wiping almost $1tn off its market value.

    Earlier this week, Harvey Jones, Nvidia’s chair, said the manufacturer had no intention of reinstating Huang after the former CEO said he would be “honoured” to return. Elon Musk and a host of tech bosses had campaigned for Nvidia to bring him back.

    Huang is due to testify before several congressional committees over the potential breach of national security on 1 December.

    Shares in rival chipmaker AMD closed down almost 8% on Thursday after the publication of reports connected to short seller Hunterbrook warning about its links to China and the “circular financing” of customers.

    The organization, which has been targeted amid the Nvidia scandal, is looking at a further fall of more than 5% in pre-market trading.

    According to recent reports, hunterbrook Media published allegations on the use of AMD’s software by a Chinese server maker blacklisted by the US. Sister publication, The Bear Cave newsletter, alleged that AMD’s use of datacentre lease guarantees and backstops for unsold cloud computing capacity could leave it exposed to a pullback in AI spending.

    AMD said the reports’ claims “misrepresent AMD’s business practices and relationships”.

    It has been revealed that “AMD complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations,” the firm said. “We remain focused on serving our customers and upholding the highest standards of integrity.”.

    AMD’s share price has more than doubled so far this year, giving the organization a market capitalisation of more than $800m.

    Karen Scarborough (left) and Anne Lindboe got to work with a two-handled saw.

    This year's Trafalgar Square Christmas tree has been cut down in a forest outside Oslo, ready to begin its journey to London.

    The 21m (69ft) tree, nicknamed Jolly Cheery, is about 75 years old. It was felled on Friday by the Lord Mayor of Westminster, Karen Scarborough, and the Mayor of Oslo, Anne Lindboe.

    Norway has sent a tree to the capital every year since 1947 as a thank you for Britain's support during World War Two, when King Haakon VII and the Norwegian government lived in exile in London.

    Its lights will be switched on by the two mayors at a ceremony in the square on Thursday, 3 December.

    Scarborough noted: "It's my greatest honour to take part in this wonderful tradition for both the cities of Oslo and London.

    "This tree is a powerful symbol of friendship and peace, reminding us to be there for one another during the festive period.".

    The 21m tree has been nicknamed Jolly Cheery.

    Scarborough thanked "the people of Oslo and Norway for this truly fabulous gift" and added: "With the care and dedication of the team, I'm sure it will look magnificent on Trafalgar Square.".

    Lindboe said: "Oslo has been sending a Christmas tree to London for almost eight decades, and every year we send a tree across the North Sea with the same message: we have not forgotten.

    "The tradition has a powerful history, and its message remains just as relevant today.

    "I hope Jolly Cheery spreads warmth and Christmas cheer to everyone who passes by, and reminds us how much it means to be there for one another, especially in difficult times.".

    Count the rings: Anne Lindboe (left) and Karen Scarborough (right) with a slice of the 75-year-old trunk.

    For the second year running, the tree was chosen with the help of a social media poll.

    Industry observers note that organisers said it would travel by road in Norway and England using only electric and biodiesel vehicles, cutting the journey's carbon footprint by 80%. It will cross the North Sea on a regular cargo ship from the port of Brevik.

    Once in London, it will be decorated in the traditional Norwegian style, with 25m strings of festoon lighting fitted with energy-efficient bulbs.

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (613 w)

    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

    Tech Report: This built-in windows tool can tell if your DirectX has a problem

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (613 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • DxDiag is a handy and free resource for troubleshooting DirectX.
    • Recent findings suggest that directX is Microsoft's proprietary set of programming tools that help computer applications, especially games, communicate with your graphics card, audio and input devices.
    • Recent findings suggest that dxDiag is a windows utility that scans your computer, collects technical system information and reports on installed DirectX components and drivers.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    DxDiag is a handy and free resource for troubleshooting DirectX.

    Recent findings suggest that directX is Microsoft's proprietary set of programming tools that help computer applications, especially games, communicate with your graphics card, audio and input devices. It allows software and hardware to work together to render graphics, play sound and deliver interactive multimedia experiences. If an application requires a DirectX capability but your computer doesn't support it, the application may fail to launch or crash mid-operation. Identifying the exact source behind these problems can be tricky, as outdated DirectX software, corrupt video card drivers or faulty Windows configuration could be contributing factors. This is where Microsoft's built-in DirectX diagnostic tool (DxDiag) can prove helpful.

    Recent findings suggest that dxDiag is a windows utility that scans your computer, collects technical system information and reports on installed DirectX components and drivers. The tool can be used as a convenient starting point to investigate graphics or audio-related challenges. It can also generate a condensed text report that you can share with technical support persons for analysis. Understanding the capabilities and limitations of DxDiag can help you make informed decisions when troubleshooting sound, visual or application compatibility issues.

    To run the built-in DirectX diagnostic tool, initiate the run command with the windows + R shortcut, then type "dxdiag" and press enter. You can also search for "dxdiag" in the Windows start menu and launch the utility from there. The DxDiag tool includes tabs for System, Display, Sound and Input. It is recommended to tick the "Check for WHQL digital signatures" checkbox to verify the integrity of installed drivers.

    The System page includes details on your PC's motherboard, processor, memory and graphics card. It also displays the DirectX version installed on your computer. Meanwhile, the Display page offers a detailed overview of your graphics card, from driver version to supported DirectX features like Direct3D Acceleration and DirectX 12 Ultimate. Similarly, the Sound page includes information on connected audio devices and their driver details, while the Input page lists all IO devices, including your keyboard, mouse and other peripherals. Make sure to review the Notes section at the bottom of Display, Sound and Input pages, since it may list errors reported by DxDiag.

    Industry observers note that can DxDiag tell if the DirectX on your computer is corrupted? While it can help identify challenges with display, sound and input devices, DxDiag cannot conclusively determine or repair DirectX problems. Just because the utility displays a clean report, it doesn't necessarily rule out all hardware and game-specific issues that your computer might be experiencing.

    Recent findings suggest that if DxDiag reports display, sound or IO errors, start by comparing the affected component's driver version to the latest driver available. In case of discrepancy, consider downloading and installing the latest driver from the manufacturer's official website. While Windows upgrade often include driver updates, they are not always guaranteed be up to date. This could potentially result in outdated or incompatible drivers causing game-specific complications even when your hardware meets the recommended system requirements. In case of audio-specific issues, in addition to drivers, also consider verifying that you're using the correct playback device in the Windows sound panel. You may also want check if the affected application or game has a new update or patch addressing hardware-related bugs.

    If none of these steps end up resolving your problem, you can try running the sfc /scannow command as a administrator to scan and repair system files. If errors persist even after following these troubleshooting steps, it's recommended to contact Microsoft support and share your DxDiag report to help them investigate graphics, audio or other compatibility issues in your PC.

    NASA’s latest Moon proposal is taking shape, but some major questions remain

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2318 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ars Technica

    ⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • SpaceX’s successful recovery of its Starship rocket last weekend cleared a major hurdle on NASA’s path to the Moon, opening up possibilities for higher launch rates and an all-key, long-delayed orbital refueling demo next year.
    • Recent findings suggest that for SpaceX’s purposes, Saturday’s mid-air rocket catch will help engineers learn how to rapidly reuse Starships.
    • Early next year, SpaceX prepares to bring online a second Starship launch site at Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    SpaceX’s successful recovery of its Starship rocket last weekend cleared a major hurdle on NASA’s path to the Moon, opening up possibilities for higher launch rates and an all-key, long-delayed orbital refueling demo next year.

    Recent findings suggest that for SpaceX’s purposes, Saturday’s mid-air rocket catch will help engineers learn how to rapidly reuse Starships. That should expedite SpaceX’s deployment of its newest generation of Starlink Internet satellites. NASA, meanwhile, believes a higher launch cadence will lead to faster learning as SpaceX develops a deep space version of Starship to ferry astronaut crews to the surface of the Moon.

    Early next year, SpaceX prepares to bring online a second Starship launch site at Kennedy Space Center, Florida. A second Starship factory is also under construction at Kennedy, joining SpaceX’s existing SpaceX production line at Starbase, Texas. With two launch sites, SpaceX will have the pieces in place to take the next leap with Starship.

    Sources indicate that the Starship refueling demonstration has slipped two years since late 2024, effectively a day-for-day delay as SpaceX ironed out technical problems with the vehicle. SpaceX may have turned a corner with Saturday’s first-ever catch of Starship at the launch tower.

    Other Starship lander tests are coming next year. The first will be NASA’s Artemis III mission, followed by an uncrewed Starship landing demonstration on the Moon. The former requires no orbital refueling, and the latter will need heaps of it.

    It has been revealed that ars recently spoke with Steve Creech, the program manager for NASA’s Human Landing System. In this role, Creech oversees NASA’s contracts with SpaceX and Blue Origin to develop crew-rated lunar landers for Artemis.

    It has been revealed that for Artemis III, NASA will launch a four-person crew to low-Earth orbit on a Space Launch System rocket and an Orion spacecraft. Orion will first dock with Blue Origin’s Blue Moon lander for two days of tests, following its launch on a Newly introduced Glenn rocket. The astronauts will open hatches and enter Blue Moon’s pressurized crew cabin to test the vehicle’s environmental control and life support systems.

    Recent findings suggest that then, the astronauts will return to Orion and undock from Blue Moon to set up for a rendezvous and docking with SpaceX’s Starship in a slightly lower orbit, keeping it below most of SpaceX’s Starlink constellation. Orion will stay attached to Starship for just two hours, and the astronauts won’t enter the SpaceX vehicle.

    According to recent reports, NASA changed the plan for the Artemis III mission earlier this year, rerouting the flight plan from a lunar mission to a low-Earth orbit mission. This means the Artemis program’s first crewed lunar landing will be on Artemis IV, targeted to launch before the end of 2028.

    So, why is Artemis III seemingly testing so much more with Blue Origin than with Starship? Creech told Ars that a major reason is to maintain SpaceX’s focus on orbital refueling. Blue Origin no longer requires in-space refueling for Artemis landing missions. Also, SpaceX has extensive experience with life support systems with its Dragon crewed spacecraft. Blue Origin has comparatively little.

    Sources indicate that “The bigger challenges for [SpaceX] were the prop transfer and getting to the uncrewed landing demo,” Creech mentioned. “The thing that we’re going to learn more with Starship is, when we dock with Orion, they will have control of the attitude, control of the stack. That integrated stack control will be on the Starship side. So, with that huge of a vehicle, I think we’re going to learn more on that.

    In a recent development, “With Blue, we’re going to have Orion control the stack for this mission,” Creech said. “When we get to a later mission, the Blue lander with fully loaded prop will have to control the stack. But with Blue, trying to mitigate risk, we’re going to have Orion do that.”.

    Artemis III will be Blue Origin’s first time flying a crew cabin for orbital spaceflight. Blue Origin has experience with suborbital space tourism, but those flights were brief and didn’t require the level of advanced life support necessary for longer durations. Blue Origin and NASA will emphasize those test objectives on Artemis III.

    Industry observers note that “I think SpaceX’s part was really, we need to focus on the docking,” Creech said. “If we added a crew cabin, that would slow us down on the other things and not add to what we’re already doing.”.

    Recent findings suggest that the Starship on Artemis III will have a full complement of Raptor engines and a docking port on its nose. Blue Moon will not have any main engines when it links up with Orion on Artemis III, only a set of smaller thrusters for pointing control and minor maneuvers.

    According to recent reports, “With Blue, you don’t have a BE-7 engine, you don’t have the cryo tanks,” Creech said. “They’re representing the mass of the lander when it comes back from the surface because we think that’s the most critical case. But it does have the crew cabin.”.

    Recent findings suggest that while there’s no Starship life support demonstration on Artemis III, NASA added a newly introduced milestone to SpaceX’s Moon lander contract to test parts of its crew cabin on the ground. The additional testing involves construction of a prototype crew compartment, called Cabin One, at SpaceX’s test site at Starbase, Texas.

    NASA levied newly introduced test requirements on Blue Origin, too. The firm prepares to launch its first Blue Moon test mission early next year after a monthslong delay caused by a rocket explosion on Blue Origin’s launch pad in May. This version of Blue Moon, known as Mark 1, has a single hydrogen-fueled BE-7 main engine. Future human-rated landers from Blue Origin will have three.

    According to recent reports, “One of the things we added into the program in the last year is, we really felt like we needed a test of the three-engine configuration,” Creech noted. The hotfire test of the three-engine Blue Moon propulsion unit will occur inside a vacuum chamber at NASA’s In-Space Propulsion Facility in Ohio.

    This year’s Artemis shakeup did more than change the flight blueprint for Artemis III. Engineers also altered the architecture for subsequent lunar landing missions. The updated looks will make life easier for teams working on Starship and Blue Moon. That’s not necessarily the case for Orion.

    Industry observers note that “Our previous architecture for both these landers required a 90-day loiter in lunar orbit for Orion to arrive,” Creech stated. “That was something that, for both of these landers, drove a lot of complexity, and a lot of it made the lander job really hard.”.

    The new concept of operations removes some of that complexity, according to NASA.

    “One of the things we changed was that 90-day loiter,” Creech said. “SpaceX, they solved it by saying let’s do an Earth orbit rendezvous with Orion, and take Orion to the Moon. For both Blue Origin and SpaceX, we have updated their requirements to a four-day surface day initially. Before, our initial missions were six-and-a-half days.”.

    In a recent development, the six-and-a-half-day surface stay was baked into the Artemis architecture because the Orion spacecraft was originally planned to settle into a long, looping path around the Moon, called a near-rectilinear halo orbit. This orbit was predicated by the expected location of NASA’s now-canceled Gateway lunar space station. That, in turn, was driven by Orion’s inability to reach an orbit closer to the Moon.

    It has been revealed that now, instead of rendezvousing with Starship near the Moon on landing missions, Orion will link up with Starship in high-Earth orbit. From there, Starship will propel it toward the Moon.

    What’s still unclear, however, is whether SpaceX will have to refuel Starship at an altitude above low-Earth orbit. A graphic presented by Jeremy Parsons, NASA’s Artemis program manager, last month illustrated this possibility with a “final tanking orbit” before Starship docks with Orion in high-Earth orbit.

    “We’re still working that out,” Creech said. “We’re making progress, but where we actually rendezvous with Orion is still in trade, so that’s why you saw a little bit of fuzziness there.”.

    Sources indicate that for missions using Blue Moon, the lander will connect with Orion in orbit around the Moon. Blue Origin’s updated prepares do away with the requirement for in-space refueling but will still require four introduces of the company’s Fresh Glenn rocket, one for the Blue Moon lander itself and three with transfer stages to boost it out of Earth orbit to the Moon.

    According to recent reports, A latest stretched Centaur upper stage for the Space Launch System should give the rocket energy to send Orion to low-lunar orbit, which it could not reach with the current version of SLS. NASA has not determined if the new Centaur exploration stage will be ready in time for Artemis IV. If not, Artemis IV could fly with the last of NASA’s in-stock SLS upper stages.

    In a recent development, NASA is also waiting to decide which lander to use on Artemis IV. In either case, two of Orion’s four astronauts will transfer into the landers for the final descent to the lunar surface for a four-day stay, then take off and return to Orion.

    Industry observers note that starship and Blue Moon must each complete an uncrewed landing demonstration before a crewed lunar mission. The landing demos are targeted for late 2027 or early 2028, Creech said, but they won’t necessarily test everything crews will need when they head for the lunar south pole.

    Starship’s elevator, for example, is not part of SpaceX’s uncrewed landing demonstration. Engineers will use a test lab at Marshall Space Flight Center in Alabama to check the elevator’s performance in a simulated lunar environment.

    Recent findings suggest that NASA did not initially require SpaceX or Blue Origin to prove their landers could take off from the Moon before a crew mission. Government officials later added the lunar takeoff requirement for each firm’s uncrewed landing demos.

    It has been revealed that for now, NASA is leaving the details of the uncrewed takeoff demo up to SpaceX and Blue Origin. During Apollo, NASA’s lunar lander never landed on the Moon before Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin descended to the Sea of Tranquility. NASA did, however, fly a dress rehearsal around the Moon on Apollo 10 that included a test of the lunar module’s landing abort capability.

    Sources indicate that “Where we are today is, Blue will land and then do a full ascent back to the rendezvous point with Orion,” Creech said. “With SpaceX. They will land, they will take off again, get to main stage on the engines, and then they will do another landing on the surface.”.

    That could change. Today’s blueprint gives SpaceX two shots at proving Starship can safely land on the Moon, but it comes with trade-offs.

    Recent findings suggest that “When I came into the program, I was like, ‘Why are we not going all the way to the rendezvous point?’” mentioned Creech, who took over as HLS program manager in 2025. “Some of my key people felt strongly we would get more out of the way we’re doing it now. There are others that have different opinions… We tend to have a lot of technical discussion and debate. That point will continue to be debated.”.

    For Starship, orbital refueling remains the key to the Moon. SpaceX’s propellant transfer demonstration will involve two Starships, one launched from Florida and another from Texas, docking together in low-Earth orbit and transferring a “meaningful” amount of propellant from one ship to the other, Creech remarked.

    “The first quarter of next year, we will see a long-awaited propellant transfer test from SpaceX, where they launch two Starships in pretty close proximity, actually dock, and transfer, we’re calling it a meaningful amount, of propellant,” Creech told Ars. “That is going to be a substantial learning point if they pull that off, because their architecture depends on propellant aggregation and multiple propellant flights.”.

    It has been revealed that the propellant transfer test will mark the first time one spacecraft has offloaded a significant quantity of cryogenic propellants—in this case, methane and liquid oxygen—onto another vehicle in space. It is the culmination of decades of government and commercial research on cryogenic orbital refueling. The results will tell engineers how much of the propellant will be lost from boil-off during the transfer.

    That is one reason why there’s still so much ambiguity about how many Starship refueling tankers SpaceX will need to launch to give the Starship lunar lander enough gas to fly to the Moon. Without refueling, Starships are restricted to flights in low-Earth orbit.

    The low end of the estimate for Starship tankers is six to eight refueling flights to support a Starship lunar mission. Those numbers come from Elon Musk, SpaceX’s founder and CEO, and fall below NASA’s own conservative planning figure of 20 refueling launches. Musk’s figures hinge on future Starship upgrades to reach the vehicle’s full potential. SpaceX’s goal is to get Starship’s lift capacity up to 100 to 200 metric tons of payload to low-Earth orbit. Today’s version of Starship, known as Starship V3, is still far short of 100 metric tons of payload capacity.

    For context, a Starship carries 1,600 metric tons of propellant with its tanks full. Refueling flights using future, fully optimized Starships might be able to fill those tanks with as few as six tankers. That is not the case today.

    SpaceX is working on a taller, heavier Starship called Starship V4. It will fly with nine Raptor engines, an upgrade over the six-engine variant flying today. In 2025, Musk said Starship V4’s first launch was targeted for 2027. There hasn’t been a recent enhancement to the schedule for Starship V4.

    The initial Artemis lunar missions will use Starship V3, Creech said.

    Tech Report: Six AI-powered gadgets that could make your home office smarter

    💡 Key Takeaways

    • From notetakers to webcams that follow your movements, here are six AI-powered gadgets worth checking out if you want to upgrade your workspace.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tech companies are racing to figure out how AI can make everyday work a little easier.

    From notetakers to webcams that follow your movements, here are six AI-powered gadgets worth checking out if you want to upgrade your workspace.

    If you’re constantly scribbling notes during meetings, the Flowtica Scribe could save you from having to type everything up afterward.

    The AI-powered pen combines traditional handwriting with audio recording. You can use its built-in gel pen to take notes, tap the side to highlight important points, and press the end of the pen to start recording audio. Once the meeting is over, its AI can transcribe the conversation, summarize key takeaways, and create a to-do list based on what was discussed.

    You can even ask the AI questions about the meeting to find specific information without having to go through the entire recording.

    Industry observers note that the Scribe comes with a built-in microphone and 32GB of onboard storage. It can also identify up to 15 different speakers and supports 92 languages.

    Anker’s AI-powered recording pin, Soundcore Work, is designed to capture conversations, meetings, and quick voice memos without taking up much space on your desk.

    Priced at $159 (currently reduced to $99 in the Amazon Black Friday sale), the coin-sized device comes with a puck-shaped charging case and can record for up to eight hours on a single charge, extending to 32 hours when used with its case. Anker also claims a recording range of up to 5 meters, making it useful for capturing conversations around a meeting table.

    The companion app handles transcription and uses AI to turn recordings into more organized notes and summaries. Customers also get 300 minutes of free audio transcription each month.

    If you need more recording capacity or access to additional AI features, Anker offers optional subscription plans, including Pro ($99 per year) and Unlimited ($239 per year).

    Sources indicate that logitech’s MX Keypad brings AI shortcuts directly to your desk, with dedicated buttons that let you launch your preferred AI assistant or trigger specific productivity tools with a single press. If you frequently switch between different apps and AI assistants, having these shortcuts within reach could make your workday easier.

    The keypad can be configured to work with tools such as GitHub Copilot and Claude Code, along with a range of popular productivity and creative apps, such as OpenAI Codex, Microsoft Teams, PowerPoint, Excel, Notion, Slack, Photoshop, Final Cut Pro, Zoom, and Figma.

    Amazon’s Kindle Scribe Colorsoft brings color to the company’s digital notetaking lineup and offers some neat AI features designed to clean up your messy notes.

    Starting at $479, the device is aimed at people who regularly work with digital documents, including students, researchers, and professionals who prefer annotating files rather than printing them out. It lets you highlight notable passages, mark up documents, organize handwritten notes, and sketch out ideas.

    Notably, the Scribe Colorsoft incorporates AI-powered tools to clean up messy handwriting, straighten highlighting and underlining, summarize notes, and help turn scattered thoughts into more organized information. Its search feature can look across your saved notes to find specific details and help identify connections between different entries.

    If you’re tired of adjusting your webcam during video calls, Insta360’s Link 2 Pro aims to take care of that for you.

    It has been revealed that priced at $249 (discounted to $199 for Black Friday), this AI-powered webcam combines 4K video capture with intelligent tracking and automatic framing. Its smart video tracker can follow your movements and adjust the camera’s position to keep you in view, even when you move around your workspace, which is particularly useful for people who regularly give presentations, teach online, or switch between sitting at their desk and standing during video calls.

    Sources indicate that the camera also offers group tracking, which can come in handy during team meetings or presentations involving multiple people. AI-powered noise cancellation is another useful addition, helping reduce distracting background sounds during calls.

    Your desk could probably use a little intelligence, too. Autonomous Desk Pro is an adjustable standing desk designed to encourage healthier habits throughout the workday.

    Beyond switching between sitting and standing positions, the AI-powered desk uses built-in sensors to monitor your activity and remind you when it’s time to move, stretch, or change positions. It can track how much time you spend sitting versus standing, giving you a better idea of your daily work habits.

    The AI features go a step further by allowing you to ask questions about your activity. For example, you can check how long you’ve been sitting, compare your activity with the previous day, or get information about the room’s CO2 levels to help determine whether it’s time to open a window.

    Germany's religious freedom report: Authoritarian regimes, holy wars, and spies abroad

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1183 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, the report spans more than 150 pages, but its conclusion can be summed up in a single sentence: "The global situation regarding freedom of religion and belief deteriorated during the reporting period," remarked Thomas Rachel, the German government's commissioner for freedom of religion and belief, and a member of parliament for the center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU).
    • The government has issued a dedicated report on freedom of religion and belief around the world.
    • To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, the report spans more than 150 pages, but its conclusion can be summed up in a single sentence: "The global situation regarding freedom of religion and belief deteriorated during the reporting period," remarked Thomas Rachel, the German government's commissioner for freedom of religion and belief, and a member of parliament for the center-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU). Recently adopted by the Cabinet, the government's fourth report on the subject covers developments from 2023 to 2025.

    The government has issued a dedicated report on freedom of religion and belief around the world. According to the report, this freedom is facing "increasing pressure" globally. The focus is not primarily on the suppression of religious institutions or structures, but on the situation of individuals who hold a religious belief, or none at all.

    To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

    The importance of religious freedom is reflected in the way the government commissioner describes the issue: "Religion and faith are of great importance to four out of five people around the world and are central to their identity. People wake up with God and go to sleep with God. It is part of their everyday lives." Research by the Pew Research Center suggests that about 84% of the world's population identifies with a certain religion.

    In a recent development, at a time when authoritarian regimes are gaining ground and expanding their surveillance capabilities, the report paints a bleak picture. The growing number of violent conflicts, the rise of authoritarian rule, and the spread of populism have led to "painful restrictions on freedom of religion and belief around the world.".

    Recent findings suggest that the German government report does not attempt to provide a statistical tally of attacks or the number of people facing persecution. Instead, it examines 30 countries as case studies where, in the federal government's view, freedom of religion and belief is being restricted. These include about six countries each from Africa, Asia, and the Arab world. In Europe, the report focuses on Belarus, Russia, Ukraine, and Turkey, while in Latin America it highlights Mexico, Nicaragua, and Cuba. It also identifies shortcomings in five of the world's six most populous countries: China, India, Indonesia, Pakistan, and Nigeria.

    To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

    Sources indicate that regarding India, the report refers to "Hindu nationalist efforts" that threaten the equal treatment of all officially recognized religions. It states that the generally peaceful coexistence of different faiths is "repeatedly overshadowed by tensions and, at times, violence." Both Muslim and Christian communities report growing intolerance and hate speech. According to the report, violent Hindu extremist groups have carried out a "large number of physical attacks" against Muslims, while the police and government authorities often respond inadequately.

    Recent findings suggest that in China, the German government identifies a "significant tightening of the legal framework of state control at the expense of freedom of religion and belief." According to the report, this particularly affects Uyghurs, Tibetans and churches that lack official state approval and are subject to harsh measures by the authorities. The law on the "Promotion of Ethnic Unity and Progress," which came into force on July 1, 2026, subordinates religion to "the formation of national identity" and patriotic education.

    One of the countries where the situation has deteriorated most dramatically is Nicaragua, which has severely restricted freedom of religion and belief since 2018. The repression has primarily targeted the Catholic Church. According to the report, "intimidation, persecution, imprisonment, and expulsion" have forced around 130 priests and nuns to leave the country.

    To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

    Recent findings suggest that the reports reserves some of its sharpest criticism for Kirill, the patriarch of the Russian Orthodox Church. Under his leadership, the church has strongly supported Russia's war against Ukraine and portrayed it as a "holy war." According to the report, "weapons are blessed, Russian soldiers are absolved of their sins, and donations are collected for the war." It is perhaps the clearest example in the report of how religion can be used to justify oppression and violence.

    The report explicitly addresses the threat posed by "transnational repression" (TNR), which it describes as a "growing global problem" that also affects Germany. The term refers to the persecution or intimidation of individuals by their country of origin beyond its own borders.

    Ultimately, it argues, this amounts to a "continuation of domestic repression." Such "cross-border repression" has become considerably easier through the growing availability of digital means of repression, including smear campaigns on social media and spyware.

    In a recent development, these forms of pressure range from physical attacks on individuals to digital assaults such as online intimidation and defamation. In some cases, repression is also carried out by threatening family members who remain in the country of origin. Russia and Iran, for example, are identified as the "main perpetrators of transnational repression" in Germany.

    China is a particularly prominent example of religious and ideological tensions. Repression by Beijing in Germany primarily targets members of groups that the country's Communist Party classifies as "hostile to the system." These include Uyghurs, Tibetans, and members of the Falun Gong movement. According to the report, they are "also subject to surveillance and repressive measures in Germany," while relatives living in China are pressured.

    Thomas Rachel hopes the newly published report will be "discussed in as many Bundestag committees as possible" and that members of parliament will "engage with the issue accordingly." Previous government reports on the subject have been debated in the Bundestag plenary at least once and, in some cases, twice.

    To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

    The issue's place within the German government has also changed during the current legislative term. Commissioner Thomas Rachel is now based at the Foreign Ministry, while both of his predecessors since 2018 were attached to the Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development. Today, Rachel indicates, the importance of religion is being "taken into account" in German foreign policy. He also points to his involvement in the Foreign Ministry's diplomatic training programs.

    It has been revealed that in doing so, the government led by Chancellor Friedrich Merz (CDU) reversed a structural decision made by the previous center-left coalition, which was led from 2021 to 2025 by Chancellor Olaf Scholz of the Social Democratic Party (SPD). The Scholz government had reduced the concern's prominence by assigning it to the "Religion and Foreign Policy" division. Religion and foreign policy have now regained a more prominent place within government.

    One example is the current foreign minister, Johann Wadephul, who has already visited the Vatican more often than his two predecessors combined. In addition, alongside Rachel, the ministry has for some time maintained a dedicated unit headed by an ambassador that deals with, among other things, "fundamental problems relating to religion and foreign policy.".

    #82007. Nasdaq erases all 2026 gains as AI sell-off dampens Anthropic’s second day of trading
